resolutions.the_defect: evals/adversarial/ledger-line-refs.json declared `files` and `min_refs` but no `input.checks`. `run_case` in src/repo_hygiene/eval_adapter.py defaulted to ["adr_headers", "adr_index"] when that key was absent, so every gate run executed two unrelated ADR checks against a clean tree and reported [PASS]. The R9 durable close did not exist: the check was written but unreachable from the gate, and the suite count moved 60 -> 61 on a case that could not fail.
resolutions.reproduced: Yes, through the runner, at 1b6c86c: breaking `tasks/TODO.md`'s ADR-021:389 ref to :399 and running `python3 -m evals.run --suite invariant` gave `[PASS] ledger-line-refs` and `invariant 61/61 = 1.000`. The tree was broken and the gate was green.
resolutions.root_cause_decision: The silent default is the root cause and it was DELETED, not guarded. Argued: the class sweep shows all 37 repo_hygiene cases except this one declare `checks` explicitly — including `adr-header-and-index.json`, the case the default existed to serve — so the default was dead behaviour whose only remaining effect was to swallow a misconfiguration as green. Adding a `checks` key to one file fixes one instance; deleting the default fixes every future case, costs nothing (nothing relied on it), and is a smaller diff than a guard clause that reimplements the same decision. `run_case` now returns a loud failure naming the case when no check is declared. Deletion over addition.
resolutions.class_sweep: All 134 committed eval cases parsed (evals/golden + evals/adversarial; report and fixture files excluded). repo_hygiene cases missing `input.checks`: ONE, `ledger-line-refs.json`, now wired. sec10k cases with an empty or missing `expect.checks` — the same cannot-fail shape on the other adapter: ZERO. `src/sec10k/eval_adapter.run_case` reads `case["input"]["path"]` directly and raises on a missing key, so it has no equivalent silent default. Sweep is clean after the one fix.

step 2, default deleted, case still unwired: `[FAIL] ledger-line-refs`, invariant 60/61 — the misconfiguration itself is now loud
step 3, `checks` key added, tree still broken: `[FAIL] ledger-line-refs`, invariant 60/61 — red for the real reason

Each provenance now states that the pre-fix red was observed by CALLING THE CHECK FUNCTION DIRECTLY, why that proves nothing about gate reachability, and records the re-observation through `python3 -m evals.run --suite invariant` with the [FAIL]/score pairs above. ledger-line-refs' claim that it 'verifies it every run' is replaced with a pointer to the wiring note, because for one commit it did not.
